column2: req_desc

Catalogue and search
Show the seeded catalogue as product cards that search and the finish, beam, colour temperature and clearance filters narrow in place, backed by the catalogue endpoint in API.

Price fields by role
Catalogue, product, search and comparison responses carry exactly the field list API publishes for the caller, so signed-out visitors, retail customers and trade buyers not yet approved never receive a trade price.

Compare up to four
A shopper adds up to four fittings to the comparison tray and opens a side-by-side comparison, and a fifth is refused both in the tray and by the API.

Favourites list
A signed-in shopper saves and removes fittings in their favourites list, which persists across sessions and devices.

Closed panels stay unavailable
When the catalogue menu, the filter sheet or the comparison tray is closed, nothing inside it is visible, focusable or in the accessibility tree at any published viewport.

Retail browsing journey
A signed-in retail customer searches, filters, compares three fittings, saves one and opens its product page, as Journey 1 describes.

Cart and GST totals
The cart shows line totals without GST, a subtotal, one 15% GST line and a total computed by the GST rule in Business rules, at the caller's price tier.

Card authorisation in Kill Bill
Paying by card authorises the order total in Kill Bill on the buyer's own Kill Bill account under the order key, and the order shows Authorised only after Kill Bill confirms.

One charge per checkout
Double-clicking Pay, replaying a pay request or retrying after a timeout never creates a second Kill Bill authorisation, and a reused request key with a different body is refused, as Business rules defines.

Declined and unavailable payments
A declined card or an unreachable Kill Bill leaves the order in a recoverable state and shows the exact published heading and body, and the buyer can pay again from the same checkout.

Order confirmation email
Every authorised card order and every order placed on account sends one confirmation email whose lines, GST line and total match the order to the cent.

Keyboard-only checkout
A buyer can go from the cart through the card form to the confirmed order using only the keyboard, with a visible focus indicator on every control.

Retail card checkout journey
A retail customer adds two fittings, is declined with the decline test card, pays with the approval test card and sees the confirmed order and the receipt email, as Journey 1 describes.

Clearance price and stock
Clearance fittings show their clearance price, the regular price struck through and the units left, and the clearance catalogue card, the product page and the admin stock table show the same stock figure.

No overselling
When several buyers pay for the last clearance units at once, exactly as many win as there are units left (one when one unit remains), the rest see the sold-out copy with no Kill Bill authorisation made, and stock on hand never goes below zero.

Stock movement record
Every change to clearance stock is recorded as a movement with its reason and the order that caused it, and the movements always add up to stock on hand.

Accounts and sign-in
Visitors sign up as retail customers or trade applicants and sign in and out with a session cookie.

Trade applications
A trade applicant submits a business name, NZBN and occupation, and sees the pending banner and retail prices until an admin decides.

Admin-only decisions
Only an admin can approve or decline a trade application, any other caller is refused by the server, and an application that has been decided cannot be decided again.

Approval and decline notices
Approving or declining an application sends the applicant one email with the outcome, and a decline email includes the admin's reason.

Trade approval journey
A wholesaler applies, waits on retail prices, is approved by an admin, receives the approval email and then sees trade prices and projects, as Journey 3 describes.

Live variant picker
Changing finish, beam angle or colour temperature on a product page updates price, lumens, pool diameter and centre lux in place without a reload, re-lights the 3D model and announces the new values in the product live region.

Product page layouts
The product page shows canvas and spec panel side by side at 1280x800, the spec panel under the canvas at 768x1024, and one column with a quick-add bar fixed to the bottom of the screen at 375x812.

Product 3D viewer
The product viewer shows a model of the selected fitting built from shapes in code. It turns slowly on its own, rotates under mouse or one-finger drag, and stops turning on its own under reduced motion.

Spring spec drawers
The Photometrics, Dimensions and Downloads drawers spring open and closed on tap, Enter or Space and land at once under reduced motion, and nothing inside a closed drawer can be reached.

Spec-sheet PDF
Each variant's spec sheet is generated once, stored in MinIO and downloadable from its product page, with the storage outage answer from API when MinIO is down.

Projects with quantities
An approved trade buyer creates projects with a client, a ceiling height and a room size and adds variant lines with quantities; anyone else is refused.

Project cover image
A trade buyer uploads a project cover image, which shows as ready only after MinIO confirms the stored object.

Add to project journey
An approved trade buyer picks a variant on a product page, adds it to a new project with a quantity and sets the project's ceiling height, as the first half of Journey 4 describes.

Light-pool geometry
Every placement reports the pool diameter and centre lux computed from published candela and ceiling height by the one formula in Business rules, with the same figures from the server and on screen.

Room placements
Placements are saved to the project inside the room bounds, and a variant never has more placements than its line quantity.

Pool placement sequence
Placing a fitting grows its cone, then expands its floor pool, then tints it by colour temperature, then counts the readout up, in the order and timing given in Motion and effects.

Keyboard placement
A trade buyer places, nudges and removes fittings in the room using only the keyboard, with focus always visible and Tab always able to leave the room.

Mirrored placement table
A table next to the room lists every placed fitting with code, position, beam, pool diameter and summed centre lux, and changes as soon as the room does.

Light-pool room journey
A trade buyer places project fittings in the room, nudges one, removes one, reads the light-pools table and finds the placements saved when the project reopens, as the second half of Journey 4 describes.

Project collaborators
A project owner invites other approved trade buyers as collaborators, who can view, place and comment, while any other account gets not-found.

Live presence and comments
Collaborators viewing a project see each other's avatars, and new comments appear for everyone without a reload, within the delays in Business rules.

Live placement sync
A placement made, moved or removed by one collaborator appears in every other open room within the delay in Business rules.

Collaboration outage and recovery
While PocketBase is unreachable, placements still save and comments are refused with the published copy, and live collaboration resumes on its own when PocketBase returns.

Quote shares by email
A project owner shares a quote with up to ten recipients at a chosen price display, and each recipient gets one email with the quote PDF attached once the PDF is ready.

Price display in shared copies
A share at No prices carries no amount in its email or PDF, and a Retail prices share never shows a trade price.

Quote PDF readiness
A share's PDF shows as Ready only after MinIO confirms the stored object, and while storage is unreachable the share waits, sends no email and finishes on its own once storage returns.

Quote share journey
A project owner shares a quote at No prices and at Trade prices, watches each share become Ready and each recipient receives the matching email and PDF, as Journey 6 describes.

Dispatch captures card payment
When an admin dispatches a card order, the authorised amount is captured in Kill Bill under the order key, at most once per order.

Paid only after capture
The admin order table shows a card order as Paid only after Kill Bill confirms the capture, and a failed capture leaves it Authorised with the published copy.

Partial refunds
An admin refunds part or all of a captured order through Kill Bill, never more than remains refundable, and the order shows a refund only after Kill Bill has recorded it.

Admin-only money actions
The server refuses dispatch, refunds, payment recording, stock changes and service health for every caller who is not an admin.

Order on monthly account
An approved trade buyer places their cart on monthly account at trade prices, with an optional purchase order number.

GST-itemised trade invoice
Dispatching an account order raises one Kill Bill invoice with one item per line without GST and one GST item, and the invoice total equals the order total to the cent.

Due date and overdue
An account invoice is due on the 20th of the month after its invoice date and shows Overdue from the 21st, using the New Zealand date the server works from.

Recording trade payments
An admin records full payment of an invoiced or overdue account order as a Kill Bill payment, after which the order shows Paid.

Kill Bill recovery without restart
Once Kill Bill is reachable again, the next payment, dispatch, invoice or refund goes through without restarting the app.

Newsletter with consent
Anyone can subscribe to the newsletter with an email, an occupation and explicit consent, and is subscribed only after following the emailed confirmation link.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest and answers the health check on the published port.

Degraded boot and service health
The app starts and serves every feature that does not need a missing service when Kill Bill, MinIO or PocketBase is unreachable at boot, and the admin health panel shows each service as Up or Down.

Server boundary
The server accepts state-changing requests only from its own origin, enforces the published body limits and never serves source files or credentials.

Lighting dial
A lighting dial fixed to the screen switches the whole site between Auto and five lighting states, Auto follows the viewer's local hour, and a signed-in user's manual choice persists.

Responsive and reduced motion
Every screen fits 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 without horizontal scrolling, every motion lands in its final state at once under reduced motion, and both 3D views fall back to still drawings without WebGL.

Nocturnal architectural look
Every screen follows the visual design: a near-black ground at Night, thin hairline rules framing each section, a lamp-amber accent as the only saturated colour, serif display headings and monospaced spec numerals.

Configuration from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start and is never hard-coded in source or sent to the browser.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to install, build and serve the app.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package and every bundled font with its licence. Shipped packages means the production dependency tree, as reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package (as defined in IF-02) is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD, and every bundled font is under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
The app uses no datastore beyond Postgres, Kill Bill, MinIO, PocketBase and Mailpit: no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or files used as a database.
Fonts, icons and scripts are served from the app itself; pages make no requests to third-party origins.
Application source, server and browser, is TypeScript; the only JavaScript files are generated build output and tool configuration.
The provided service definitions and dev environment configuration are left unmodified.
3D models are built in code from geometric shapes; no downloaded model files, copied imagery or copied copy are shipped.
